scope: Approved typed field capability API restructuring and caller migration; no publication or dependency pin update.
root_cause: Rich generic field method sets instantiate optional row/selected/aggregate capability families and promoted concrete/pointer wrappers for each owner/value/scope combination.
The existing email/template path links text/template reflection; MethodByName retention increases linked public-method reachability. Compiler archives are already large before linking.
The inspected 1552.3 MiB historical datatable archive contained only about 68.7 MiB of machine instructions; symbol/string/relocation/export metadata dominated.
Overlapping test/export/development builds amplified peak resource use; race and changed-source variants require separate cached artifacts.
implementation: Stored-field Value, Param, CountField, CountDistinctField, Min, Max, Sum and Avg are opt-in typed functions with sealed data descriptors.
Concrete source type parameters avoid the prototype's extra interface boxing allocation. Common predicates/order/group/write methods remain fluent.
Scalar/binary shared storage is data only. Existing AST, codecs, compiler, executors and transaction contracts remain the shared owners.
Framework/application handwritten callers, generator examples, compiler-negative cases and native editor probes are migrated. Generated output is checked through its existing owner.

conditions.cache: Existing warm cache; never cleared or replaced.
conditions.workload: Existing productionprofile with typed self-join/nullable fields, exact numeric summary and the standard email template engine. API syntax migrated without changing workload.
conditions.measurement_limits: Static artifact comparisons are matched. Final build reused compiled artifacts; no wall-time or final compiler-RSS speedup is inferred from cached versus uncached phases.

runtime_benchmarks.interpretation: Full query-building timings were similar (~14.5 microseconds) with unchanged allocations/bytes. Individual function microbenchmarks cost approximately 16 ns more than former methods in this sample; no database throughput claim.
runtime_benchmarks.rejected_interface_prototype: The first free-function prototype added 80 bytes and one allocation per full workload; concrete source constraints removed this regression.

compiler_contracts.initial_result: Only seven expected diagnostic substrings were stale; actual intended rejections remained enforced. The corrected cases passed, and the final full source gate reran the catalogue.

operational_conditions: An existing application development watcher started an automatic rebuild during an early verification attempt. Its rebuild was stopped and watcher paused; early mixed-run timings are not controlled comparisons.
A later temporary guard refused new stages while another chat's Go race test was active; no competing benchmark was launched.
Subsequent stages use sequential Go execution and a start-time process guard. The two previously paused CLI chats require human resume.
After all controlled checks completed, the existing development watcher was resumed; its existing application server remained running.
limits: Large typed ORM test compilation still requires multi-gigabyte compiler memory; this is a measured reduction, not elimination of generic compilation cost.
The warm cache retains old and new source/race variants, so total cache size is not expected to fall immediately.
No full cross-platform/race or independent published-version adoption is claimed. Current local PostgreSQL/Redis and the selected native editor/application checks are recorded separately.
The versioned application framework pin remains unchanged; its migrated callers require the matching unpublished local workspace until user-managed publication/adoption.
post_gate_documentation: After make verify, only a Value documentation comment was clarified; runtime signatures and behavior are unchanged. Native editor and application checks used this final source.
